Free Fatty acid content of the ghee should be less than 0.5%, more than 3% is considered poor quality
           NDDB CALF report (Sr.No) is showing 0.44%

Stearic acid levels are high in animal fats, but the report is showing (NDDB CALF Sr No.23) is showing 9.6 (within the range between 8 and 19). Stearic acid should have been abnormally high if the ghee is adulterated with animal fats.
Iodine value (indicator for saturated fat) is also in the acceptable range, Animal fats are saturated fats, you could expect much lower Iodine value if the ghee is adulterated with animal fat
Saponification value (NDDB CALF Sr.No #47) is slightly higher 
Report shows 241 but the range is 205-235

         The whole confusion is coming from Annexure 1
         S-Value and equations
        There are 5 equations : 3 of them showing the samples are OK and other             
         two equations are showing around 20

If the S value of 20 is correct, there is no justification in NDDB CALF report Stearic acid levels are in good shape, iodine value is in the good range and free fatty acids are below 0.5%

NDDB CALF report showing S-value and Annexure 1 values are confusing.
NDDB CALF Sr. No 13 Lauric acid levels are quite high 
Lauric acid is 11.71 (the range is 1.5-4.0)
It is definitely coming from usage of coconut oil 
Coconut oil contains high levels of lauric acid

BASED ON THE REPORT THE PRODUCT IS ADULTERATED WITH VEGETABLE OILS NOT WITH ANIMAL FATS
